title: TSV keep-out rings fused with segmented deep-trench storage capacitors
idea: Combine the HBM TSV and the cell capacitor: etch an annular deep trench (AR ~50) in the dead keep-out zone around each TSV, split it into 16-32 sectors with vertical dielectric fins, and use each sector as a storage capacitor read through vertical transistors on the ring rim. One structure is the TSV stress shield, a decoupling cap and bit storage.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): turns the ~10-15% of die lost to TSV fields and keep-out zones into bits; claimed +5-8% bits per HBM core die plus free decap.

title: Hybrid-bond pads double as sense-amp coupling capacitors
idea: In a wafer-on-wafer DRAM (array wafer face-bonded to a CMOS wafer), leave a 2-3 nm oxide in the Cu-Cu bond pads that carry 16:1-muxed local bitlines, so each pad is both the interconnect and the coupling capacitor of a charge-transfer preamp on the logic wafer. The bond needs no DC continuity, and the logic-side sense amp runs at 0.5 V.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7) and voltage floor (fact 10): sense amps leave the array wafer; low-voltage sensing claimed ~2x lower sensing energy and ~25% smaller array die.

title: CCD fused into 3D NAND-style string: vertical shift-register DRAM
idea: Combine a charge-coupled device with a 3D NAND gate stack: 200 tier gate planes wrap one vertical oxide-semiconductor channel, and clocking the gates shifts charge packets held in surface wells toward a floating-diffusion sense node at the top. Each gate is both 'capacitor' and transfer switch, so there is no per-cell capacitor, contact or access transistor.
why: No 3D cell (fact 2) and charge wall (fact 1): ~0.1 fF wells suffice because the floating diffusion has gain; one hole etch stores 200 bits. Serial latency ~100-200 ns, hidden by striping each cache line across 512 strings.

title: Coaxial hole: capacitor sheath below, gate-all-around transistor above
idea: One high-AR hole per 4F2 site does both jobs: the lower ~80% is lined as a cylinder capacitor (plate/high-k/storage shell), and the top ~20% passes through a deposited wordline plane where a channel-all-around transistor joins the storage shell to a top bitline. Gate length is set by wordline-plane thickness, so capacitor and transistor share one etch and one alignment.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 4F2 (about 33% less area than 6F2) with full-height capacitor and no storage-node contact or landing pad, deleting ~2 critical litho layers.

title: Silicon interposer fused with deep-trench DRAM banks
idea: Combine the passive 2.5D interposer under GPU+HBM with memory: fill its 2,000-3,000 mm2 with 40-65 nm deep-trench eDRAM (AR ~80) plus interposer-native refresh and sense logic, so the wiring substrate is also a multi-GB near-memory tier.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and HBM shortage: uses depreciated legacy fabs, no EUV; ~2,500 mm2 at ~0.06 um2/bit gives ~3-5 GB per package at mm-scale wire lengths (fact 5).

title: Passing-gate trenches become shield lines that back-bias neighbors
idea: Combine row-hammer shielding and leakage control in one buried trench: every passing-gate buried wordline is replaced by a line held at about -0.5 V that both screens active rows from aggressor coupling and back-gates the adjacent access channels into deeper off-state.
why: Row hammer (fact 9) and leakage tail (fact 3): removes the passing-gate hammer path (threshold up >10x) and cuts GIDL/subthreshold tail ~10x for ~4-8x longer refresh; area cost offset by deleting hammer-tracking logic.

title: Two bonded array wafers share one sense-amp plane
idea: Bond two DRAM array wafers face-to-face with the sense-amplifier layer at the bond plane: each SA's true bitline lies in the upper array and its complement in the lower one, combining open-bitline density with folded-bitline noise cancellation because both halves see the same vertical coupling.
why: Periphery (fact 7): one SA row serves two arrays, halving SA area per bit; 4F2-compatible with folded-like margins; ~20-25% die area per bit cut.

title: Display backplane fab fused with DRAM: panel-scale memory sheets
idea: Combine an oxide-TFT display backplane line (3 m Gen-10.5 glass, ~1.5 um rules, a storage capacitor already in every pixel) with DRAM: print 4 stacked tiers of 1T1C cells with small local subarrays, then dice the panel into capacity-tier CXL memory sheets.
why: Cost per bit and capital (fact 4): display area costs ~100x less per m2 than DRAM wafers; ~14 um2/bit x 4 tiers gives ~360 GB raw per panel, targeting <$2/GB for a 100-300 ns capacity tier.

title: Subarray sense amps fused with micro-ring optical modulators
idea: Bond a photonic wafer over the DRAM array so every subarray's local sense-amp row drives silicon micro-ring modulators directly; the latched bit biases the ring's PN junction, and global bitlines, I/O muxes and SERDES become one WDM waveguide bus running over the mats.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and overfetch (fact 8): claimed <1 pJ/bit array-to-processor versus 3-4 pJ/bit HBM, and bank-level parallel optical channels.

title: Hollow TSVs that are also microfluidic coolant channels
idea: Make annular TSVs whose copper shell carries power/signal while the hollow core carries a two-phase dielectric coolant through the whole stack, combining vertical interconnect and cooling in one via field.
why: Lets compute sit on DRAM (fact 5) while holding DRAM <=60 C; retention roughly doubles per ~10 C, so refresh energy (fact 3) falls 2-4x and 24-32-high stacks become thermally feasible.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM fused with bonded defect-routing mesh
idea: Never dice: keep a whole 300 mm DRAM wafer, hybrid-bond a router-mesh wafer above it (Cerebras-style), and route around bad mats, so the wafer, package and module become one ~1 TB memory plane fed by edge optical links.
why: Removes dicing, packaging, TSVs and KGD test (fact 6); ~100% of good mats usable after sparing; cost per bit claimed -20-30% and ~1 pJ/bit on-wafer transport.

title: Cell layout co-designed with block-copolymer hexagonal lattice
idea: Combine directed self-assembly and the vertical-channel cell: put transistors and capacitors on the natural hexagonal lattice of a cylinder-forming block copolymer, with zig-zag wordlines and 60-degree bitlines matched to that symmetry, so one coarse guide exposure plus self-assembly defines the array.
why: Litho and capital (fact 4): replaces 2-3 EUV layers; hex packing at pitch 2F gives ~3.5F2 per cell versus 6F2 (~40% denser).

title: Backside power network fused with DRAM periphery
idea: Borrow logic backside power delivery for DRAM: move VPP/VARY/VDD rails and charge-pump capacitors to the wafer backside through nano-TSVs, freeing frontside metal for 2x bitline/local-IO tracks and letting row-decoder strips tuck under the mats.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and voltage floor (fact 10): periphery area -20-30%, lower IR drop allows tighter VARY margins; die area per bit -10-15%.

title: Bonded SRAM sector buffers fused with segmented wordlines
idea: Hybrid-bond a thin SRAM/logic layer so each 1 Kb wordline segment has its own SRAM sector buffer at the bond site; an activate opens only one 64-bit segment and the buffer serves column hits, merging row buffer, cache and wordline segmentation.
why: Overfetch (fact 8): activation energy per useful bit drops ~8-10x (about 5.9 to ~0.7 pJ); fewer full-row activations also lowers hammer exposure (fact 9).

title: Capacitor-boosted 2T1C gain cell for thin lateral 3D tiers
idea: In each lateral 3D tier, combine a 0.5-1 fF short horizontal capacitor with a separate read transistor whose gate is the storage node; the capacitor only has to hold that gate's charge between refreshes, not drive a bitline.
why: Charge wall and 3D blocker (facts 1-2): lateral capacitors 5-10x shorter, tiers ~40 nm thick so 100+ tiers are plausible; read is nondestructive (fact 8).

title: Antiferroelectric-ferroelectric bilayer capacitor parks idle rows nonvolatilely
idea: Stack antiferroelectric ZrO2 (linear-like, unlimited-endurance charge storage) with a thin ferroelectric HZO in one capacitor: active banks store bits as AFE charge, and when a bank idles the controller 'parks' each row into FE polarization, stopping refresh until the next access.
why: Refresh (fact 3): idle-bank refresh power (16-33% of idle) to ~0; FE layer switches only on park/unpark (~10^6 cycles per day budget).

title: DRAM tiers and NAND tiers sharing one CMOS-under-array stack
idea: Combine a 3D DRAM tier block and a 3D NAND tier block above the same CMOS-under-array die, sharing staircases and page buffers, so pages migrate between DRAM and NAND tiers internally at TB/s without crossing an I/O pin.
why: Do DRAM's job with less DRAM: cold pages demote in-die, so a system needs maybe 30-50% fewer DRAM bits; data movement (fact 5) for swap traffic nearly eliminated.

title: Cross-die shared redundancy pool for stacked memory
idea: Combine stack interconnect with repair: rather than each die carrying its own spare rows and columns, pool spares on one die (or spread across the stack) and remap failing rows of any die through the base die's TSV/bond network with a content-addressable remap table.
why: HBM yield (fact 6, 20-30% loss): stack-level sparing rescues dies that fail per-die repair, raising stack yield ~10-15 points and trimming per-die spare area 2-3%.

title: Wafer bonding fused with monolithic tiers: four wafers of 32
idea: Combine both 3D routes: each wafer carries a 32-tier monolithic memory stack (aspect ratio manageable in one etch), and four such wafers are hybrid-bonded to one periphery wafer, giving 128 tiers without a 128-tier etch.
why: 3D break-even (fact 2, ~26+ tiers): reaches 128 tiers with 4 moderate etches; etch AR stays <40:1, raising yield and cutting high-AR etch tool time.

title: Vertical wordline makes each activation span tiers, not rows
idea: Combine tier count with page size: in a 3D array with vertical wordlines and per-tier horizontal bitlines, an activate opens one pillar's cells in all 64-128 tiers, each tier landing on its own sense amp at the staircase edge, so a page is 64-128 bits by construction.
why: Overfetch (fact 8): ~64-128x less activation per useful bit (activate share <0.1 pJ/bit); row hammer (fact 9): logically adjacent rows are separate pillars, not coupled neighbors.

title: Wordline drivers built on the 3D staircase steps
idea: Combine the 3D contact staircase with the X-decoder: deposit thin-film transistors directly on each staircase tread so every tier's wordline driver and pre-decoder sits on its own step, turning dead staircase area into periphery.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and 3D cost (fact 2): removes decoder strips and long fan-out wires; ~8-12% die area recovered.

title: Vertical bitline pillar with built-in preamp transistor at its base
idea: Merge the local sense preamp into each vertical bitline of a 3D DRAM: a gain transistor whose gate is the short vertical bitline converts the charge-share signal to current before it reaches the long global bitline.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): with ~0.2 fF vertical bitline, a 1 fF cell transfers ~83% of its signal, so cells need ~1 fF instead of 5 fF; enables short lateral capacitors and 100+ tiers (fact 2).

title: Series-stacked array voltage domains recycle bitline charge between tiers
idea: Combine two arrays (bonded tiers) in series between 0 and 2xVARY: the upper array swings VARY-2VARY and its restore current returns through the lower array swinging 0-VARY, recycling charge like stacked-voltage logic, with the scheduler balancing activations.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): ~40-50% of array CV2 supply energy recycled without lowering VARY; fewer pumps shrink periphery (fact 7).

title: Deposition-defined 3D DRAM patterned only with US micron-scale steppers
idea: Combine 3D NAND's thickness-defined geometry with a DRAM cell: gate length, capacitor gap and tier pitch are all set by film thickness on US-built ALD/CVD/etch tools, and the only lithography is a ~1 um hole/slit grid from US-made i-line steppers, halved by one spacer pitch split. Density comes from ~300 tiers in 3 decks and 4 cells around each hole, not from imported EUV or immersion scanners.
why: Litho and capital (fact 4) and US manufacturability: zero EUV; 0.25 um2 per hole / (4 cells x 300 tiers) is ~2e-4 um2/bit, about 4x 1-beta density.

title: Cymer-laser interference lithography plus Multibeam e-beam cuts for arrays
idea: Combine maskless two-beam 193 nm interference lithography (ArF lasers built in San Diego) for the perfectly periodic wordline, bitline and pillar gratings with US multi-column e-beam direct-write (Multibeam, Santa Clara) for the sparse cuts, contacts and periphery, plus one spacer doubling to reach ~20 nm half-pitch.
why: Fact 4: removes 5-7 EUV layers and the photomask set; interference tool estimated <$10M; e-beam writes only the ~5% irregular features, so throughput stays workable for an all-US flow.

title: Nanotwinned copper pads enable 150 C bonding of heat-sensitive memory tiers
idea: Fuse (111)-oriented nanotwinned copper, electroplated from US-mined copper on US-built plating tools, into hybrid-bond pads; its fast surface diffusion forms Cu-Cu bonds at ~150 C, so finished AFE-capacitor or thin-film-transistor memory tiers can be stacked repeatedly without retention-damaging 300-400 C anneals.
why: 3D tier count (fact 2): cumulative thermal budget no longer caps bonded stacks; enables 8-16 bonded memory wafers per stack with domestic inputs.

title: Molybdenum-dioxide electrodes template rutile TiO2 for short lateral capacitors
idea: Combine a rutile-structured MoO2 storage electrode (from Colorado molybdenum) with ALD TiO2 so the dielectric grows in its rutile phase (k ~80-100) below 400 C, with light Al doping to curb leakage, replacing imported Ru/RuO2 templates and k~40 ZrO2.
why: Charge wall (fact 1, needs k~70): ~2x k makes lateral 3D capacitors ~2x shorter for thinner tiers; element chain Mo/Ti/Al is fully domestic.

title: Mo wordline surface sulfurized into its own MoS2 channel
idea: Combine wordline and channel from one element: after each 3D tier's Mo wordline and an ALD HfO2 gate dielectric (Oregon hafnium), a thin Mo film on top is sulfurized below 450 C into 2-3-layer MoS2, giving a self-aligned, atomically thin access channel per tier.
why: Facts 2-3: ~1.6-1.8 eV few-layer MoS2 cuts off-leakage below Si and a 2 nm channel keeps tiers thin; all-US supply (Climax Mo, refinery sulfur, domestic Hf) and no indium/gallium.

title: Wolfspeed SiC access-transistor wafer bonded onto silicon periphery
idea: Fuse a power-electronics material into memory: build the access-transistor and capacitor array on 200 mm 4H-SiC in a US wide-bandgap fab (Wolfspeed, New York), then hybrid-bond it to a US silicon CMOS periphery wafer; SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by orders of magnitude.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): refresh interval from 64 ms toward seconds-hours, removing 16-33% idle power and 10-20% bandwidth loss; adds an existing domestic fab to memory supply.

title: MEMS micromirror process fused with DRAM: nano-relay access switches
idea: Replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nano-cantilever relay built in a back-end sacrificial-gap MEMS flow like TI's Dallas DLP micromirror line; the open contact is a vacuum gap, so off-state leakage is essentially zero, and the relay sits above its capacitor in the same 4F2 footprint.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): no subthreshold or GIDL path, retention limited by dielectric leakage (minutes+), refresh almost gone; nm relays switch in ~10-50 ns, contact endurance (>10^15) is the risk.

title: Capillary self-alignment fused with hybrid die-to-wafer bonding
idea: Pattern hydrophilic bond-pad fields and hydrophobic die rims so a thin water film self-centers each DRAM die to <0.5 um by surface tension before Cu-Cu bonding, letting fast, simple US-built pick-and-place replace imported precision hybrid bonders.
why: HBM stacking (fact 6) and US manufacturability: ~10x throughput and ~5x lower tool cost than precision die-to-wafer bonders made abroad; supports 16-24-high domestic stacks.

title: Harvested server DRAM dies restacked with sidewall-metallized interconnect
idea: Combine e-waste recovery with 3D stacking: dies desoldered from retired US hyperscaler DIMMs are retested, thinned, given an RDL that routes pads to one edge, glued into 8-16-high cubes, and wired together by laser-patterned metal on the lapped cube sidewall (Irvine Sensors-style), assembled at US OSATs.
why: Raises usable supply with near-zero wafer capital or scarce materials: retired DDR4/DDR5 dies become dense CXL capacity cubes; no TSVs (fact 6).

title: Shingled die staircase with vertical bond-via wires replacing TSVs
idea: Fuse NAND-style offset die stacking with free-standing vertical copper wire arrays (US-developed bond-via-array): each DRAM die is shifted to expose an edge pad row and molded ~50 um-pitch vertical Cu wires rise from the substrate to every die, built on Arizona OSAT lines.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSVs, keep-out zones or TSV yield loss, recovering much of HBM's ~3x area-per-bit penalty; stack cost ~30% lower at ~3x DDR5 package bandwidth.

title: Photonic HBM base die from a US silicon-photonics foundry
idea: Merge the HBM logic base die with optical transceivers built at a US photonics fab (e.g., GF Fotonix, Malta NY): DRAM cores stack on a base die that speaks WDM over fiber, so the stack needs no 2.5D interposer beside the GPU and can sit centimeters to meters away.
why: Removes dependence on offshore CoWoS interposers and frees placement for more stacks per accelerator; ~1-2 pJ/bit links versus 3-4 pJ/bit HBM (fact 5).

title: Array wafers from one US fab, periphery wafers from another, bonded
idea: Split DRAM across domestic fabs: array-only wafers (capacitors, access devices, few metals) at a US DRAM fab, periphery CMOS on depreciated 28-45 nm US logic/analog lines (e.g., TI Lehi, the former 3D XPoint fab), fused by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding on US soil.
why: Capital (fact 4) and periphery (fact 7): the costly DRAM fab spends all tools on bits (~2x bits per DRAM-fab wafer) while idle US logic capacity builds periphery; array die area per bit about -40%.

title: Memory tier slipped into Intel 18A backside-power stack
idea: Fuse logic backside power delivery with memory: after the US PowerVia flow thins the wafer, deposit a low-temperature capacitor plus thin-film-transistor memory tier on the backside between the transistors and backside power rails, giving each logic die tens to hundreds of MB of DRAM-class memory microns from its cores.
why: Data movement (fact 5): <0.1 pJ/bit vertical access; absorbs cache/KV traffic so accelerators need fewer HBM bits; built in existing US leading-edge fabs.

title: Polycrystalline diamond bond layer doubles as interlayer heat spreader
idea: Combine bonding dielectric and heat spreader: grow ~1 um CVD diamond (US-built reactors, methane/hydrogen feedstock) on DRAM wafers, polish it, and use it as the bond layer between a hot logic die and DRAM tiers so hotspots spread laterally before reaching the cells.
why: Enables logic-on-DRAM stacking (fact 5) while keeping DRAM below 85 C (refresh doubles per ~10 C, fact 3); diamond ~1,000 W/mK versus 1.4 for SiO2; all-domestic inputs.

title: CTE-matched molybdenum TSVs dropped inside the cell array
idea: Fill TSVs with domestic molybdenum, whose ~5 ppm/K expansion nearly matches silicon, so stress keep-out zones shrink from ~10 um to <1 um and TSVs can sit inside the subarray grid (in sense-amp gaps) instead of dedicated TSV channels.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): reclaims ~5-10% die area, avoids China-dominated tungsten and Cu-pumping yield loss, and allows more channels per stack.

title: Pulsed-laser-crystallized silicon tiers stacked monolithically above periphery
idea: Combine the display industry's laser crystallization with 3D DRAM: deposit amorphous Si for each tier and melt-crystallize only its top ~100 nm with nanosecond pulses from US-made laser sources, keeping lower tiers and CMOS below 400 C and giving near-single-crystal access channels tier by tier.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2): monolithic tiers without wafer bonding or Si/SiGe epitaxy (no imported germanium); crystalline mobility for lateral transistors at the cost of one deposition plus laser pass per tier.

title: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled 3D DRAM with 1 fF lateral capacitors
idea: Fuse rack-scale LN2 cooling (US air-separation plants, no imports) with a 3D lateral array designed for 77 K: leakage falls by >10^6, so 1 fF short horizontal capacitors still retain for seconds, tiers become ~5x thinner and refresh nearly disappears.
why: Facts 1-3: capacitor wall sidestepped, refresh (46 fJ/bit) near zero, and wire resistance ~5x lower at 77 K (fact 5); cryo plant cost amortized per rack.

title: Reconstituted known-good array dies bonded wafer-to-wafer onto periphery
idea: Combine fan-out wafer reconstitution with wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding: tested good array dies are placed into a reconstituted 300 mm carrier at a US advanced-packaging center (e.g., SkyWater Florida), planarized, then bonded in one step to a periphery wafer.
why: 3D/HBM yield (fact 6): W2W throughput without compounding yield loss, since bad array dies never kill good periphery; ~15-25% more good stacks per wafer pair.

title: Backside-illuminated sensor thinning fused with double-sided trench DRAM
idea: Reuse the CMOS-image-sensor flow at a US 300 mm fab (onsemi East Fishkill, the old IBM trench-DRAM site): etch full-depth deep-trench capacitors, thin the wafer to ~3 um as in BSI sensors, and contact capacitor plates and power from the backside while access transistors and bitlines own the front.
why: Facts 1 and 7: plate/strap contacts and power leave the front side (~20% tighter cell pitch); trench depth is fixed by thinning rather than etch AR; revives domestic trench know-how for a capital-light line.

title: Boron-doped etch-stop superlattice replaces SiGe for lateral 3D DRAM
idea: Build the 3D DRAM tier stack as single-crystal Si epitaxy with alternating heavily boron-doped layers (US borate supply) instead of Si/SiGe, then remove the p++ layers with a dopant-selective HNA-type wet etch to open lateral capacitor and channel cavities, using no germanium.
why: 3D blocker (fact 2) and scarce resources: germanium is largely China-sourced; Si/Si:B has near-zero lattice mismatch, so less strain and more (100+) tiers, all domestic.

title: Area-selective ALD self-aligns storage-node landing pads, deleting masks
idea: Combine area-selective deposition with the landing-pad step: inhibitor molecules adsorb on dielectric but not on contact plugs, so Mo/TiN grows only on plugs and mushrooms into self-aligned landing pads on US ALD tools, removing the landing-pad lithography.
why: Fact 4: deletes one of the 5-7 EUV layers and an overlay-critical step (~5-8% wafer cost), making a non-EUV US flow more viable.

title: National open 3D-DRAM pilot line fused with shared PDK at Albany
idea: Combine the Albany NY public R&D fab with an open, licensable 3D-DRAM process design kit: startups and universities tape out cell and array variants on shared multi-project wafers, and CHIPS money buys tier-stack and bonding tool sets whose recipes transfer to US production fabs.
why: Capital and time (fact 4): entry cost for a new US memory architecture drops from ~$1B to ~$1-5M per experiment, speeding the 3D cell search (fact 2).

title: Molybdenum wordlines double as in-field annealing heaters
idea: Combine the wordline with a micro-heater: during maintenance windows, pulse current through domestic Mo buried wordlines (replacing Chinese tungsten) to Joule-heat a mat to ~250 C for milliseconds to seconds, annealing hydrogen-related interface traps behind variable-retention-time leakage and weak cells.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): shrinking the <=13 fA tail could double or more the refresh interval (refresh energy halved) and heal hammer-induced trap damage (fact 9); thermal stress on neighbors is the risk.
